αἰγανέῃσιν: αἰγανέη — light javelin, hunting-spear; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσιν (= Attic -αις)
γενεῇ: γενεή — birth, lineage, descent; fem. dat. sg.: ’by birth’
γυναικῶν: γυνή — woman; fem. gen. pl., partitive with δῖα: ’heavenly-one of women’ · also partitive with ἀρίστη: ’best of women’ · also possessive gen. with a noun: ἔργα γυναικῶν ’the works of women’ · also gen. after a verb of surpassing, ’above, beyond women’ (περίεσσι γυναικῶν) · also gen. pl. dependent on a noun of speech, ’of … women’ (φάτιν ἀνδρῶν ἠδὲ γυναικῶν ’the talk of men and of women’) · also fem. gen. pl., partitive with indefinite τις: ’one of the women’ (τις … γυναικῶν) · also fem. gen. pl. in apposition with δμῳάων: ’women (servants)’ (γυναικῶν δμῳάων ’women servants’)
δίσκοισιν: δίσκος — discus; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις), dat. of means: ’with discuses’
δεινοῦ: δεινός — dread, awful, terrible; masc. gen. sg., agreeing with θεοῦ
δωδώνην: Δωδώνη — Dodona, seat of the oracle of Zeus in Epirus; fem. acc. sg.
δῖα: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; fem. nom. sg., epithet of goddesses and heroes
εἰδότες: οἶδα — know; perf. part. masc. nom. pl.: ‘knowing’
εἶδος: εἶδος — form, look, beauty; neut. acc. sg. (accusative of respect): ’in beauty’
εὔμηλος: Εὔμηλος — Eumelus, a man of Pherae, husband of Iphthime; masc. nom. sg. · also εὔμηλος — rich in flocks, well-flocked; adj., fem. nom. sg., two-ending (of an island)
ζωὸς: ζωός — alive, living; masc. nom. sg.
θήβης: Θήβη — Thebes; fem. gen. sg., with ἕδος: ’seat of Thebes’
κάτα: κατά — down, throughout; prep. + acc., placed after its noun with anastrophe: κραναὴν Ἰθάκην κάτα ’throughout rocky Ithaca’ · also standing after its verb, not after a noun: ἔχῃ κάτα δῆμον ἅπαντα ’holds throughout the whole land’ (κατά + acc., or tmesis for κατέχῃ)
καθύπερθεν: καθύπερθεν — from above, on top; adv. · also prep. + gen.: ’above’ (Ὀρτυγίης καθύπερθεν ’above Ortygia’)
κακῷ: κακός — bad, base, ignoble; masc. dat. sg. · also of smoke: κακῷ … καπνῷ ’foul smoke’
καλλιγύναικα: καλλιγύναιξ — with fair women; adj. (2-term.), fem. acc. sg., agreeing with Σπάρτην
κεῖτ: κεῖμαι — lie; impf. 3 sg., elided (κεῖτο → κεῖτ’ before a vowel): ’lay, was lying’
κεῖτο: κεῖμαι — lie, be laid; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔκειτο): ’lay’
κρατέρ: κρατερός — mighty, strong, harsh; neut. acc. pl., elided (κρατέρ’ = κρατερά)
λίμνην: λίμνη — mere, standing water, lake; fem. acc. sg.
λίπον: λείπω — leave, leave behind; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= Attic ἔλιπον)
λωτὸν: λωτός — lotus, the lotus plant and its fruit; masc. acc. sg.
μάχοντο: μάχομαι — fight; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἐμάχοντο): ’were fighting’
μέδων: Μέδων — Medon, herald of Odysseus’s household; masc. nom. sg.
μέλαινα: μέλας — black, dark; fem. nom. sg.
μήλων: μῆλον — sheep, small cattle; neut. gen. pl.
μενεπτόλεμος: μενεπτόλεμος — steadfast in battle (μένω + πόλεμος); masc. nom. sg.
μνήσεσθαι: μιμνῄσκω — remind; mid. remember, be mindful of (+ gen.); fut. inf. mid.: ’to be mindful’
μογήσας: μογέω — toil, suffer hardship; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having suffered’
μοῦσα: Μοῦσα — Muse, goddess of poetic inspiration; voc. sg. · also nom. sg. (same form), subject: ’the Muse’ (Μοῦσα λίγεια ’the clear-voiced Muse’)
νῶτον: νῶτον — back; neut. acc. sg. (usually pl. νῶτα)
οἰκί: οἰκία — dwelling, house; neut. pl., elided (οἰκί’ = οἰκία)
οἷσιν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; possessive adj., neut./masc. dat. pl. (ν-movable): ’his own’ (agreeing with δώμασιν) · also relative, masc./neut. dat. pl.: whom (λαῶν οἷσιν ἄνασσε), not the possessive
οὗτοι: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; masc. nom. pl.: ’these’
πέλασσεν: πελάζω — bring near; aor. 3 sg., epic -σσ-, unaugmented (= ἐπέλασεν), + dat.: ’brought (me) to’
πήλιον: Πήλιον — Pelion, mountain in Thessaly; neut. acc. sg.
παραὶ: παρά (epic παραί) — beside, along; prep. + dat.
παῖδε: παῖς — child, son; masc. acc. dual: ’two sons’
πειριθόοιο: Πειρίθοος — Peirithous, king of the Lapiths; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ποθέοντες: ποθέω — long for, yearn; pres. part. masc. nom. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ποθοῦντες)
πρώτιστον: πρῶτος — first; superlative πρώτιστος; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’first of all’
πτολιπόρθῳ: πτολίπορθος — city-sacking, sacker of cities; masc. dat. sg., epic πτολι- (= πολι-)
στυγὸς: Στύξ — the Styx, the underworld river by which the gods swear their most binding oath; fem. gen. sg.
τέκετο: τίκτω — beget, bear; aor. 3 sg. mid., epic, unaugmented (= ἐτέκετο), said of a father: ’begot’
τέμενος: τέμενος — sacred precinct, plot of land set apart; neut. nom. sg.
τέρποντο: τέρπομαι — take pleasure, enjoy oneself; impf. 3 pl.
τείχεα: τεῖχος — wall; neut. acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic τείχη)
τόξων: τόξον — bow; neut. gen. pl. (τόξα), ’bow, bows’
τὰς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. pl.: ‘them, those’ (referring to ships) · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the mules · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the cattle · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the fruits · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the nymphs and of the Sirens · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: fem. acc. pl. ’which’ (ἀπειλάων, τὰς … ἐπηπείλησε ’threats which he threatened’) · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the swine · also fem. acc. pl. with ἄλλας, article-like: ’the others’ (τὰς δ’ ἄλλας ’and the other (portions)’) · also fem. acc. pl. with a noun, article-like: ’the, those’ (τὰς κούρας ’the maidens’) · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the goats · also fem. acc. pl. ’them’, of the small birds · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: fem. acc. pl. ’whom’, of the maidservants (τὰς … ἔργα διδάξαμεν ’whom we taught tasks’)
υἱέας: υἱός — son; masc. acc. pl., epic υἱέας (= Attic υἱούς/υἱεῖς)
υἷε: υἱός — son; masc. acc. dual: ’two sons’
φέρτατος: φέρτατος — best, mightiest; superl. of φέρτερος, masc. nom. sg.
φιλοκτήτης: Φιλοκτήτης — Philoctetes, the Greek archer at Troy; masc. nom. sg.
φοίτων: φοιτάω — go to and fro, come repeatedly; impf. 3 pl., unaugmented, uncontracted (= Attic ἐφοίτων): ’were coming’
ἀγλαὸς: ἀγλαός — splendid, radiant; masc. nom. sg.
ἀθάνατος: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; adj., masc. nom. sg.
ἀνάκτων: ἄναξ — lord, master; masc. gen. pl. (θεῶν ἀνάκτων ’of the lord gods’)
ἀνθεμόεντα: ἀνθεμόεις — flowery, rich in blossoms; masc. acc. sg.
ἀποθρῴσκοντα: ἀποθρῴσκω — leap up from, spring up; pres. part. acc. sg. masc.
ἀπορρώξ: ἀπορρώξ — broken-off piece, hence an outflow, trickle; fem. nom. sg.
ἀργυρότοξος: ἀργυρότοξος — of the silver bow; masc. nom. sg., epithet of Apollo
ἀρείων: ἀρείων — better, braver; comparative of ἀγαθός (cf. ἄριστος); masc. nom. sg.
ἀτρεΐδῃσιν: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus (Agamemnon, Menelaus); masc. dat. pl., epic -ῃσιν (= Attic -αις)
ἀχέων: ἀχέω — grieve, mourn; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic (cf. ἄχνυμαι): ’grieving’
ἄντιφος: Ἄντιφος — Antiphus, son of Aegyptius; masc. nom. sg.
ἄρισται: ἀγαθός — good; superlative ἄριστος ’best’; fem. nom. pl. ἄρισται, predicate: ’best, foremost’
ἅρμασιν: ἅρμα — chariot; neut. dat. pl. (pl. for a single chariot)
ἅρματα: ἅρμα — chariot; neut. nom./acc. pl. (pl. for a single chariot)
ἐγχεσιμώρους: ἐγχεσίμωρος — spear-wielding, spear-fierce (second element disputed: linked to μῶρος ’eager, mad’ or to μέμονα ’be eager’); masc. acc. pl., stock epithet of the Myrmidons
ἐλέλειπτο: λείπω — leave; plpf. 3 sg. pass.: ’had been left (over)’
ἐξείλετο: ἐξαιρέω — take out, take away; aor. mid. 3 sg.: ’took out’
ἐρεπτόμενοι: ἐρέπτομαι — feed on, munch; pres. part. mid. masc. nom. pl., + acc.
ἐτίσατο: τίνω (mid. τίνυμαι) — pay, requite; mid. exact vengeance, take vengeance on; aor. 3 sg. mid.: ’took vengeance (on)’
ἐϋκτιμένην: ἐΰκτίμενος — well-built, well-founded; fem. acc. sg., epic ἐϋ- (= εὖ); said of a town or house, and of a tilled plot
ἐών: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic ἐών (= Attic ὤν), accented ἐών before a pause: ’being’ (τοῖος ἐών ’being such’)
ἑλλάδα: Ἑλλάς — Hellas, here a district of Thessaly; fem. acc. sg.
ἑπτὰ: ἑπτά — seven; numeral, indecl. (ἑπτὰ καὶ δέκα ’seventeen’)
ἔβαλεν: βάλλω — throw, hurl; aor. 3 sg., ν-movable: ’threw’ (κὰδ … ἔβαλεν = κατέβαλεν ’threw down’)
ἔλαιον: ἔλαιον — olive oil; neut. acc. sg.
ἔννεπε: ἐννέπω — tell of, relate, speak; pres. imper. 2 sg.
ἔτεκεν: τίκτω — bear, beget; aor. 3 sg., augmented
ἔχεν: ἔχω — have, hold; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= εἶχεν): ’held’
ἕστασαν: ἵστημι — stand; pluperf. 3 pl., intransitive, with simple past force: ’were standing’ (reduplicated ἑ-στα-σαν)
ἡγήσαιτο: ἡγέομαι — lead the way, guide (+ dat.); aor. opt. 3 sg., purpose after ὡς: ’might lead’ · also potential with ἄν: ’would lead the way’ (καὶ ἂν πάϊς ἡγήσαιτο ’even a child could lead’)
ἡγείσθην: ἡγέομαι — lead, go before; impf. 3 dual: ’the two led’
ἡγεμόνος: ἡγεμών — guide, leader; masc. gen. sg.
ἰδὲ: ἰδέ — and; epic conj. (= Attic καί)
ἱέντες: ἵημι — throw, hurl, let fly; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’throwing’
ὀλοόφρονος: ὀλοόφρων — baleful-minded (sense of this epithet, e.g. for Atlas, is debated; perhaps ’all-knowing’); gen. sg.
ὁπλότερος: ὁπλότερος — younger; comparative adj. (superl. ὁπλότατος); masc. nom. sg.
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὑπερθύμοιο: ὑπέρθυμος — high-spirited (ὑπέρ + θυμός); masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ὕδατός: ὕδωρ — water; neut. gen. sg., accented before an enclitic
